To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cold phase of the interstellar medium is not present at HI column densities below $N_{HI}=2\times 10^{20}~cm^{-2}$, and that this threshold is likely due to inefficient self shielding of the neutral gas from the ultraviolet interstellar radiation field.

the fraction of HI gas in the cold phase is a decreasing function of HI column density below $2\times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$; this threshold is consistent with self-shielding of HI against ionizing photons.

the cold neutral medium is formed at HI column densities $N_{HI}\ge 2\times 10^{20}\, \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ and that the warm neutral medium is the dominant phase at lower column densities, $N_{HI}< 2\times10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical conditions of the cold neutral gas in the Galaxy.
the physics of the interstellar medium (ISM) and how it affects the formation of stars.
the physical conditions that determine the fraction of the cold neutral component in the interstellar medium (ISM), and the role of the warm neutral medium in regulating the formation of the CNM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a HI column density threshold exists below which the formation the CNM is inhibited.
the HI column density at which the cold gas forms is $N_{HI}=2\times 10^{20} cm^{-2}$.
the threshold in HI column density is a result of the interplay between the self-shielding of HI and the formation of the CNM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CNM is a rare phase of the neutral medium, which is formed at HI column densities above $2 \times  10^{20} $ per cm$^{ 2}$.
the cold phase of gas in the Galaxy is formed in the presence of high HI column densities, and the warm phase is formed at lower HI column density.
the CNM is a self-regulated phase of gas that is only present when the HI column density is high enough for the gas to self-shield against ultraviolet radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HI column density threshold of $N_{HI}=2 \times 21$ per cm$^{squared}$ can be used to distinguish between warm and cold neutral media.
the HI column density is an important parameter in the physics of cold gas formation, and that it should be included in future theoretical models of the interstellar medium.
a threshold in HI column density exists below which gas is predominantly in the warm neutral medium, and above which gas is predominantly cold.
